quest.title: Where Does Her Name Rest?
quest.description: Seek her name within the boundless sea called "the past"...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1225, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act VI
chapter.title: Melting Moonlight in the Morning Mist

talks.objective: Go through the gate Nicole opened once you are ready

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I have confirmed that you are all in good health. With that, my work is now complete. Congratulations are in order.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are these people...?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Judging by their clothes, they appear to be phantom Hyperboreans from the distant past.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That could mean they have some clues about the Moon Goddess's name, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, could you tell us what the Moon Goddess's name is?

dialogues.speaker: Xsayazantus
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, sorry. That's probably a weird question, huh... How do we explain this?

dialogues.speaker: Xsayazantus
dialogues.text: The moons are long gone, and their goddesses are dead. Their names no longer mean anything.

dialogues.speaker: Xsayazantus
dialogues.text: When a new Moon Goddess is born, we will surely know her name.

dialogues.speaker: Xsayazantus
dialogues.text: We have used every last resource at our disposal. All that remains is to wait, patiently and quietly...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Were the people of the past all this devout? Hmm. It looks like this phantom doesn't intend to converse with us any further.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Surely, the new Moon Goddess he speaks of must be Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Alas, Kuutar's birth came long after the age in which he lived.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Salvation did not come.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm... But, um... Maybe if we... find a phantom from a more recent age, they might know Columbina's real name?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: True. Keep an eye out. We should be able to tell which era they're from by the clothes they wear.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nicole? Nothing to say on the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... You've been pretty talkative this whole time.... What changed?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Oh... Nothing, I'm fine. You all make good points.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: When the Hyperboreans speak of moon goddesses, they mean the three from truly ancient times. I can't imagine they would know anything about our current Moon Goddess.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: There once was a time when the moon goddesses blessed them greatly and protected them from harm. So, when the war between the gods and dragons plunged the world into chaos, it seems they looked once more to the moons for help, praying for a new goddess to be born.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that checks out.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Let's continue on. Who knows what else we may discover.

talks.objective: Examine the painting on the wall

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, there's a whole bunch of artwork in here... Seems pretty old. Nicole, this is probably your area of expertise — what do all these paintings mean?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Let me see... Hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: To understand these murals requires some knowledge of the history surrounding the war of funerary flame. I shared a little of this with Lauma before.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Hmm... Yes, I think I follow. The dispute between the moon sisters, the transformation by Nibelung...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Oh, no, it's no trouble! I'd be delighted to share the tale again!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A—Alright then...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Teyvat's three moons and their goddesses were brought into being by the will of Nibelung, the then-ruler of Teyvat.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: But when the Heavenly Principles came, they changed the world completely, down to its very foundations.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: The moon goddesses were nowhere near strong enough to challenge this entity. But the Heavenly Principles did not view them as heretical entities that had to be removed.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Essentially, the three moons existed to keep this planet alive and operational, which did not directly conflict with the Heavenly Principles' aims. Nevertheless, the inherent precariousness of this arrangement would soon be revealed...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Nibelung returned, yes?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: He did, and thus began the war of funerary flame. A battle for dominance between Nibelung and the Heavenly Principles.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Discord would soon emerge between the three moon sisters. One would voice the opinion that they should follow Nibelung, for it was he who first hung the moons in the sky.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Another would argue that taking sides in the conflict would only bring the world closer to ruin. There was no telling where it would lead.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Especially since their creator had returned bearing the perilous power of the Abyss.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Nibelung would eventually discover their disloyalty. He had all three imprisoned before transforming the moons into weapons with which to fight against the Heavenly Principles.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Weapons!?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Yes. The very moons that had once defended the planet became instruments of death and destruction, striking terror into the hearts of all living things.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: And although the Heavenly Principles and the three moon sisters had once been at peace, it now seemed that the moons posed an unacceptable threat to Teyvat.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: It is possible that the Heavenly Principles did not know of the goddesses' imprisonment. If so, the weaponization of the moons would surely have been viewed as an intentional breach of the peace agreement.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What happens then?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Regardless of who knew what when, the Heavenly Principles shattered two moons, and flung the other beyond the skies.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Whether the goddesses managed to escape Nibelung's captivity after his fall, nobody knows.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: But this much is certain: From that day on, the moons no longer belonged to Teyvat. The rejection slowly drained their power until eventually, they passed away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's the full story...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: You say the moons ceased belonging to Teyvat from then on. Why, then, would Columbina be born here?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: That is perhaps due to the lingering connection between the Frost Moon, which was not shattered, and this world. You could see it as the three sisters' dying wish.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: They never desired war. All they ever wished for was to protect this land.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: ...I see.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: If the final fate of the three goddesses is as you say, then Columbina faces the same grave danger.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Our investigation has yet to bear fruit. We must hurry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're right. Let's keep going!

choices.text: Maybe it's one to save for when we get back?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: They... didn't make it...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: My name...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you tell me your name?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you tell me your name?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: My name... is...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Columbina!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Columbina!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're finally here... Guessing we'll need to activate this thing?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Indeed. I was a little worried about that at first, but as we got closer, I sensed that the kuuvahki within it flows unimpeded. It should be functioning normally.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: The only issue is how to activate it... It's looking a little worse for wear...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: What about the cores from some of the other devices we've seen? Can we repair it using those?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: In all likelihood, yes. I imagine that would have been the Hyperboreans' backup plan. Let's look for some cores.

talks.objective: Find a way to activate the device

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: This is where the people of Hyperborea communicated with the moons.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: We need only place the Moon Marrow upon this platform on Moon-Prayer Night, and we shall be able to open a portal to the moon and send our Moon Goddess back home.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: The assumption being, of course, that we can find her first.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: That's right... You want to know if it's safe there, don't you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Exactly. It might have been corrupted by the Abyss.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: And yet she has no choice but to return. You know this.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's not the only issue here... This is the end of the line, right? We've explored everything we can.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But despite looking at historical artwork and talking to people from Hyperborean times... We're still no closer to learning Columbina's name.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Hmm... If it's not too much trouble, could you tell me exactly what Alice said to you about "finding her name"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, sure. What she said was...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Then your first job is to find it. As a Moon Goddess, I'm sure she must have a name she identifies with.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Neither "Columbina" nor "Kuutar" is her true name, and she's never really accepted either of them.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: ...Is it not also possible that... She has never had a true name? Not at any point in history?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: That would be a hard pill to swallow. But at this point, we may have to accept that that is the truth.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: No one knows how she came into being, and she certainly doesn't have "parents" in any sense that we're aware of. Perhaps... she was never granted a name at all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... Does that mean there's no way to get Columbina back? She's just gonna disappear, and there's nothing we can do about it?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Huh...? Wait... Why all this pessimism? Was it the way I phrased this question? You all seem to be taking this in completely the wrong way...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What do you mean by that...?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Well, just because she's never had a real name in the past doesn't mean she can't have one now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...What?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Think about what Alice said again. She never once said that you'd have to find a "new" name, did she?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Are you saying what I think you're saying?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You want us to grant her a name?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Yes. Names are anchors that connect us to the world. If she doesn't have one already, then all we have to do is create one! No?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: #It's like... Ah, yes! {NICKNAME}, when you first arrived in Teyvat, do you think you would have turned around if someone behind you shouted out "Hey, Tumaini!"

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No, I wouldn't...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: And now?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I understand what you mean.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Life is a long journey. Even the friends and family by our side can change over time.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: When people call you by different names, what matters isn't so much the words themselves, but what they symbolize.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: And of course... whether that resonates with you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Lumine...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Aether...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: So, close your eyes and picture the Moon Goddess in your mind. If you were to call out to her in this moment, what would you say?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Columbina...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Columbina.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon would call her Columbina too.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: She has long forsaken everything that "Kuutar" represents... I think... from now on, I should call her Columbina, too.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Well, it sounds to me like you've found your answer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you sure? Is it really that simple? We haven't found her this whole time, and not for lack of trying!

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: For a journey like this, the process is every bit as important as the outcome.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Had you not searched far and wide, rejecting every other answer you were offered, how could you have come to an answer you felt was finally correct?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Ohh! It all makes sense now... This has Alice's fingerprints all over it...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Are you suggesting that mage knew from the start that Columbina never had a real name to begin with?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Um... I can't say for sure. But I can definitely imagine her chuckling in satisfaction somewhere right now, saying, "Ah, what fun!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lauma! Your antlers!

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: ...You should hurry. The festive moon has begun to rise.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Do not worry, for when you called the name "Columbina" just now, I could sense that the power within was enough to summon back the moon goddess.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The power within what? The name...?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Yes, so... the thing is... Ugh... Gah!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Umm... What's wrong now?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: This is so annoying! Gah! I really, really, really want to explain how that whole thing works! Starting from the founding principles of Teyvat, and... Oh, I could talk about this for hours!

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: But...! Deep breaths, Nicole, deep breaths. You're an angel, a sober, sensible, solemn angel who has her priorities straight!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Okay then. Sorry for asking. Clearly a bad call on Paimon's part.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: ...Anyway! You all need to hurry! Last thing: Remember how it felt when you called out that name.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Then it is agreed...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: By the name "Columbina" we shall find her...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then we'll throw her the best Moon-Prayer Night party ever!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And at last, we will send her home.

choices.text: The moon is... beyond the sky, right?

talks.objective: Enter the gate that has been opened

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I... can barely move anymore...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: My consciousness... is fading away...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Have they come back out? I... I'd love to see them one more time...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Columbina Hyposelenia. That's a wonderful name.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I never thought that "Columbina" would become my real name.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: But after I met you, and my other friends, the things that this name stood for slowly began to change.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: It went being from a Fatui codename... to "something my friends call me."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (How much she's changed since we first met... She never used to share her innermost thoughts.)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Hmm? What is it? Why aren't you saying anything?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm just so happy for you.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Hehe, thank you. So, where's everyone else?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We can go and meet them very soon. Everyone went to different places to try calling your name.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Great. I'd like to thank them as well. Everyone's done so much for me — searching for my name, entering those ancient ruins...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, so you were...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Yes, I was there. Not physically, but my consciousness was still holding on. I followed you the whole way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Starting from when?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: You turned around and called out my name while you were in Nasha Town. Do you remember?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Ah, so that's what that was...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I could've sworn I felt someone pat me on the back... And deep down, I think I knew that it was Columbina.)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Let's go. We don't want to keep them waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure. In that case, come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Ah, but...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Before that... Could you call my name one more time?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Haha...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure. Come with me, Columbina Hyposelenia.

talks.objective: Bring Columbina with you and meet up with your companions

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Columbina spreads the good news to your friends by way of small animals and kuuhenki...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: But since not everyone speaks critter sign language, some friends took longer than others to get the message.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: It's good to know you're all well. Puts me at ease.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Columbina! Are you here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Columbina! Are you here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Columbina... That's the name you gave when we first met

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Columbina... That's the name you gave when we first met

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And it's what I've called you ever since

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And it's what I've called you ever since

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Columbina...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's a fine name

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's a fine name

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I have many fond memories of Columbina...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I have many fond memories of Columbina...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And so do all of your friends

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And so do all of your friends

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If you like this name...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If you like this name...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Looking for me?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I like it

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You can carry on using it

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: My name is:

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Columbina Hyposelenia

dialogues.speaker: Xsayazantus
dialogues.text: When the moons rise again, we shall receive their protection once more...

dialogues.speaker: Xsayazantus
dialogues.text: Even in the darkest hour, there is always a way out...

dialogues.speaker: Hufarna
dialogues.text: The moons have left for now... but they would not abandon us forever...

dialogues.speaker: Examine Bookshelf
dialogues.text: (The shelves are stacked with books. Unfortunately, none are related to the birth of a new Moon Goddess, and there is no mention of a "Columbina.")

dialogues.speaker: Zarinia
dialogues.text: Should we trust him to keep his promise?

dialogues.speaker: Artaraye
dialogues.text: We have to. There's nothing else we can do.

dialogues.speaker: Rayagaos
dialogues.text: Why? Why do the creators of this world no longer show mercy upon their people?

dialogues.speaker: Manuxsathes
dialogues.text: Remember his words... we must change our fate... with our own hands...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Wait, that's odd... Who is... "he"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: No, not really. It's just that over thirty possibilities emerged in my head, so I can't be sure who "he" is... It's been too long. My memory isn't as sharp as it once was.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, okay... Thirty, wow... Impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After informing your friends, everyone splits up to look for Columbina by calling her name.\nYou choose to visit the place where you first met...
